title: sre-source-route-leak-postmortem-2026-03-18
body:
Summary:

On 2026-03-18 at ~02:07 UTC we observed partial loss of control-plane connectivity from a small subset (~3%) of private deployment clusters in eu-west-1. Symptoms: API latency spikes followed by 502s from the control-plane agent, customer-data plane unaffected for most workloads, but operator actions (rollout, sync) failed intermittently. Total user-visible impact window ~42 minutes for affected clusters.

High-level impact:
- Affected: 4 customer clusters on Dedicated/private VPCs (different customers)
- Control-plane agent health checks failing intermittently; kube-apiserver reachable from within node namespace but not from the control-plane collectors
- No data exfiltration or workload crashes observed

Timeline (concise):
- 02:06 UTC: automated alert — control-plane API error rate rising (SLO signal).
- 02:07–02:20 UTC: oncall paged; initial triage by oncall (Ethan) — ruled out pod restart storm. Observed high RST counts in control-plane collectors.
- 02:22 UTC: Priya identifies asymmetric routing on one customer gateway (source-route present) via tcpdump and next-hop table mismatch.
- 02:28 UTC: Mitigation attempt — applied temporary policy to force symmetric path (policy id: temp-policy-2309) on the edge router; partial recovery for two clusters.
- 02:39 UTC: Correlation with recent firewall rule push from customer management plane (ticket JIRA-SRE-1372) that modified edge NAT behavior.
- 02:48 UTC: Permanent rollback and additional route filters deployed via infra PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842).
- 02:53 UTC: Metrics normalized; incident declared mitigated at 02:55 UTC. Post-incident monitoring until 03:30 UTC.

Root cause hypothesis (final):
A recent automated firewall management change (customer-initiated) created an ACL/NAT combination at the customer edge that introduced asymmetric source-based routing for traffic from our control-plane collectors back to the control-plane endpoint inside the customer VPC. Specifically: the control-plane collector IPs were SNATed behind a different egress interface, and return path policies on the customer gateway insisted on a different next-hop for that source range, causing packets to be dropped or RSTed when connection tracking did not match. The combination of a) new ACL ordering, b) an SNAT change in our edge NAT config pushed during a simultaneous rollout, and c) the customer's strictly pinned routing on their on-prem gateway produced transient connectivity failures.

Contributing factors:
- Edge NAT rollout (infra PR 842) coincided in time with the customer's firewall rule change; lack of a cross-checking preflight in our rollout pipeline allowed the simultaneous change.
- Existing health checks for control-plane paths only tested single-direction reachability; we did not exercise return-path symmetry checks.
- Oncall runbook didn't include a quick diagnostic for asymmetric routing (no tcpdump guide for gateway pairs).
- Customer gateway had very strict reverse-path filtering configured (rp_filter strict), which amplified the impact.

Detection and diagnostics (what we ran):
- kubectl logs on control-plane agent pods (collector) — saw frequent "connection reset by peer" and TCP RST counts.
- tcpdump on edge router and inside customer gateway VM to compare SYN and SYN-ACK paths. Command examples used:
  - sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.4.12.9 and port 6443 -w /tmp/collector.pcap
  - sudo tcpdump -i bond0 src 44.55.66.77 and dst 10.4.12.9 -vv
- ip route show table all on edge routers and customer gateway; noticed different main vs. policy routing tables.
- conntrack -L | grep 44.55.66.77 showed many entries with state=ESTABLISHED then quickly deleted.
- netstat -tnp | grep 6443 to confirm connection attempts and RST flags.

Mitigation steps taken (live):
1) Scoped temporary policy to override customer's egress SNAT for collector IP range (temp-policy-2309) — restored symmetric path for two clusters.
2) Rolled back our simultaneous NAT change and pinned collector source IPs to a stable egress pool.
3) Coordinated with customer network engineer to relax reverse-path filtering temporarily and to accept the collector source range.
4) Deployed route filters to ensure that return traffic from the control-plane endpoint uses the same path back to our collectors (infra PR 842 rollback + patch).

Why the mitigation worked:
- Restoring SNAT consistency and removing the unexpected ACL ordering removed the asymmetry; RSTs stopped because conntrack entries were no longer mismatched.

Permanent remediation and action items (owners / due dates):
- infra: add preflight check in NAT rollout to detect overlapping customer ACLs and to block simultaneous edge NAT changes when customer-managed firewall changes are detected (owner: Jared; due: 2026-04-05).
- eng-private-deployments: add symmetric-path health probe to control-plane monitoring (SLO probe) that validates SYN+SYN-ACK on both edge and customer side (owner: Priya; due: 2026-04-01).
- runbooks: create "asymmetric-routing" diagnostic checklist with tcpdump templates and quick mitigation commands (owner: Asha; due: 2026-03-25).
- support: update customer onboarding docs to include a section on reverse-path filtering and expected NAT behavior (owner: Customer Success; due: 2026-04-10).
- security: review policy that allows infra NAT changes to be coord-suppressed with customer firewall pushes (owner: Security Eng; due: 2026-04-07).

Runbook draft snippets to add (quick wins):
- Diagnostic command set (to paste in pager):
  1) tcpdump on our edge: sudo tcpdump -i <edge-if> host <collector-ip> and port <api-port> -c 200 -w /tmp/edge.pcap
  2) tcpdump on customer gateway: sudo tcpdump -i <cust-if> dst <collector-ip> and port <api-port> -c 200 -w /tmp/gw.pcap
  3) ip route show table all; ip rule list; iptables-save -t nat | sed -n '1,120p'
  4) conntrack -L | grep <collector-ip> | tail -n 50
  5) curl -v --connect-timeout 3 https://<control-plane-endpoint>/healthz --interface <collector-ip>
- Quick mitigation checklist:
  * If asymmetric routing detected: pin collector SNAT to stable pool (rollback NAT), coordinate with customer to add host route for collector range, or temporarily relax rp_filter if customer agrees.
  * If mitigation requires customer action, escalate to Solutions Eng and Customer Success with templated message (include pcap and trace ids).

Communication notes (what we told customers):
- Initial message: "We're investigating intermittent control-plane API errors affecting a small number of clusters in eu-west-1. Engineers are working on a network path issue and will follow up with details." (02:15 UTC)
- Follow-up: error cause identified as routing asymmetry with suggested temporary relaxation of reverse-path filtering; coordinated rollback performed. (02:45 UTC)
- Final: Confirmed mitigation and follow-up actions assigned; offered post-incident call for impacted customers. (03:10 UTC)

Post-incident analysis items (deeper follow-up):
- Replay packet captures to confirm exact packet loss timeline and retransmit behavior (owner: Ethan; due: 2026-03-22).
- Add synthetic tests for return-path validation in CI for private deployments (owner: Platform Eng; due: 2026-04-12).
- Investigate adding a small BGP/route-validation shim that detects non-symmetric policy changes and flags a preflight failure (owner: Routing Team; due: 2026-04-30).

Appendix (raw snippets):
- sample ip rule output that helped identify the problem:
  32766:     from all lookup main
  32767:     from all lookup default
  32763:     from 44.55.66.0/24 lookup custom-edge

- tcpdump excerpt (SYN without matching SYN-ACK on return):
  02:11:03.123456 IP 44.55.66.77.51874 > 10.4.12.9.6443: Flags [S], seq 12345678, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
  02:11:03.124890 IP 10.4.12.9.6443 > 44.55.66.77.51874: Flags [R.], seq 87654321, ack 12345679, win 0, length 0

- helpful references: internal runbook stub: confluence: /display/SRE/Asymmetric+Routing+Diagnostics (draft)

Notes / lessons learned (TL;DR):
- Asymmetric routing between our collectors and customer control-plane endpoints can manifest as RSTs and rapid conntrack churn; SNAT and ACL ordering are common triggers.
- Prevent simultaneous edge NAT changes when customers push firewall changes; implement preflight checks and a small maintenance window coordination system.
- Add active symmetric-path checks to control-plane SLOs to catch this class of failures earlier.

If you have questions or want raw traces, see attached artifacts in the JIRA ticket or ping #sre-oncall.
